subject.title: [Bug]: Subagents can appear completed before the underlying delegated work is actually finished

question: Should subagent task completion remain tied to child agent-run terminal state while child-owned background exec/process sessions are surfaced separately, or should child-owned process liveness gate subagent completion?
rationale: Both behaviors are plausible product contracts: blocking on every process can strand intentional detached work, while the current separation can still make parent sessions believe delegated work is done too early.

options.title: Surface Background Work Separately
options.body: Keep child agent-run completion authoritative, but make child-owned process sessions visible in tasks/session status and parent handoff so users are not told all delegated work is done.

options.title: Gate Completion On Process Liveness
options.body: Treat scoped child-owned background process sessions as part of subagent completion with bounded timeout, cancellation, cleanup, and explicit detached-work escape rules.

options.title: Document Current Semantics
options.body: Clarify that subagent completion means the child agent turn ended and that background processes must be tracked through process/task status, accepting the current behavior as intentional.

recommendation.title: Surface Background Work Separately
recommendation.body: Keep child agent-run completion authoritative, but make child-owned process sessions visible in tasks/session status and parent handoff so users are not told all delegated work is done.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the best available routing owner because the decision spans recent subprocess hardening and subagent lifecycle behavior, and the current alternatives require maintainer product judgment.
